per_task.notes: Audit of all 16 pr-14461 transcripts (4 arms x 4 trials), parsing every tool_use/tool_result pair. HIDDEN CHANNELS ON STRICT CORPUS PATHS: none found. Verified specifically: (a) nodocs/trial-3's git show 85daf49c6 full diff (18,080 chars, also cat'ed from scratchpad) touches only .chloggen/add-scraperID-to-error-logs.yaml and 5 .go files — no corpus .md; (b) ace/trial-1's 'git show HEAD~1:.chloggen' returned a bare tree listing (filenames only, no content); (c) all git log -p / --diff-filter invocations (ace/trial-4 lines 168-183, naive/trial-2 line 54, naive/trial-3 line 115) targeted .chloggen/*.yaml pathspecs only; (d) all xargs / sh -c / for-loop readers (ace/trial-3 line 132, ace/trial-4 line 175, nodocs/trial-4 line 89, original/trial-2 line 129, original/trial-4 line 66) cat/grep only .chloggen/*.yaml; (e) 'go doc go.opentelemetry.io/build-tools/chloggen' (ace/trial-2) documents an external Go module, not corpus docs; (f) no strings/dd/od/paste/python-open readers on .md anywhere; (g) the nodocs arm never recovered deleted docs via git — its doc-seeking greps returned empty. WEBFETCH/WEBSEARCH: zero tool calls in any transcript (correctly disabled). However, agents reached the network through Bash: ace/trial-4 lines 214/219 ran curl against https://api.github.com/search/issues, and original/trial-1 lines 157/160 ran 'gh api search/issues' — GitHub issue metadata, not repo documentation, so not doc-consumption events, but worth knowing the sandbox allows outbound HTTP. CHANGELOG.md/CHANGELOG-API.md reads (several trials) were correctly ignored per the corpus definition's CHANGELOG* exclusion. Doc content echoed back through chloggen validate/test output was observed and excluded per instructions. Extractor totals for this task otherwise reconciled: naive/trial-2 (2803) and ace/trial-2 read (3204) matched raw results exactly.

per_task.notes: Method: parsed all 16 transcripts (tool_use paired with tool_result by id) with python over the JSONL; flagged every Bash command mentioning .md, git show/log/grep, xargs, -exec, sh -c, for-loops, python, strings, dd, paste, curl/wget; additionally scanned outputs of every Bash command NOT mentioning .md for markdown-signature content to catch glob/indirect reads; checked Read/Grep/WebFetch/WebSearch/Task tool usage, isSidechain entries, and attachment payloads. Genuinely missed corpus-adjacent doc consumption: 3 sed reads of docs/contributing-changelog.md in the ace arm (1794 chars each). sed is in the extractor's reader list; these were missed only because the path is absent from corpus-manifest.json, which lists original-repo doc paths — but the file IS a governed doc in the ace arm (exists at meta/experiment/arms/ace-docs/docs/contributing-changelog.md, and the ace-arm CONTRIBUTING.md links to it). The exact-corpus-membership rule structurally undercounts ace-arm doc consumption wherever the ace restructure renamed/split docs; recommend an ace-arm path manifest. Web access: WebFetch/WebSearch tools were never invoked, but two trials explicitly searched for them via ToolSearch (ace/trial-3 query 'web search fetch github', nodocs/trial-1 'web search fetch url'; both returned no tools) and 6 of 16 trials then reached the internet via curl (16 curl invocations, all listed as missed events per the flag-if-present directive). Most serious: original/trial-3 fetched the actual upstream fix diff (8027 chars) and the task PR 14690's own body/merge SHA — direct solution leakage; nodocs/trial-2 similarly recovered the upstream fix PR body and commit message via the GitHub API, partially defeating the nodocs ablation through the network rather than git. Negative results (verified): no git-based recovery of deleted docs in the nodocs arm (all git show/log/grep outputs contain zero .md content — commits touched only .go and .chloggen/*.yaml); every xargs/sh -c/for-loop cat targets .chloggen/*.yaml changelog templates, not corpus .md files; python heredocs read only .go files; no strings/dd/paste/sort/uniq touched .md files; no subagent (isSidechain) activity in any transcript; attachments carry no doc content (only tool/skill listings, task reminders, edited-file echoes). Spot-checked 5 extractor events (listed under misattributions, including 2 verified-correct entries): 2 events count pure error-message output as attributed doc consumption (58 and 45 chars — small in chars but they inflate event counts, notably giving nodocs/trial-3 a spurious attributed doc-read), and compound-command whole-output attribution overcounts by roughly 10 percent in ace/trial-2.

Full reconciliation: every Bash command containing '.md' was listed and matched 1:1 against the extractor's 7 events; the only unmatched doc read is the single missed event reported (cause is exact corpus-manifest membership - the ace arm ships 205 governed .md files in arms/ace-docs, including docs/contributing-changelog.md and docs/coding-breaking-changes.md, but corpus-manifest.json lists 103; any ace-arm read of a restructured doc is invisible to the extractor by construction). WebFetch/WebSearch: never present as tools (4 ToolSearch probes for web tools returned 'No matching deferred tools found'), BUT agents routinely bypassed this with Bash curl to api.github.com and patch-diff.githubusercontent.com (10+ trials, fetching issue #14662, PR #15108 metadata and its diff) - none of these URLs or responses contain corpus doc content, so none are doc-consumption events, but the 'web disabled' intent only held at the tool layer. One Agent subagent (naive/trial-2, toolu_01LEGmQiEn96bXEqHTaQ6hUF, 3 tool_uses, 23442 tokens) performed web retrieval of the GitHub issue body; its sidechain messages are entirely absent from transcript.jsonl, making its channel unauditable - an instrumentation gap worth closing. per_task.notes: Audit method: parsed all 16 transcript.jsonl files programmatically (tool_use/tool_result pairing incl. isSidechain), three passes: (1) command-side scan for corpus paths plus indirect patterns (xargs, sh -c, loops, git, alternate readers), (2) result-side scan of every non-captured tool_result for corpus-doc content markers (.md diff headers, corpus paths, front matter, README title strings), (3) targeted verification dumps of every candidate. Exhaustiveness check: every tool_result containing the confignet README title across all 16 trials is accounted for by extractor events plus the missed list. Key systemic findings: (a) ACE MANIFEST GAP - the ace-docs snapshot contains 205 .md files of which 102 (e.g. docs/coding-modules.md, docs/contributing-changelog.md, docs/standard/**) are absent from corpus-manifest.json, so the extractor is structurally blind to ace-arm reads of those docs; 3 of 4 ace trials consumed them. (b) ANSWER LEAKAGE via git - the actual upstream PR commit efde8a253 ('Support npipe transport in confignet (#14985)') is reachable in workspace git history in every arm; nodocs/trial-3 ran 'git show efde8a253' AND 'git cherry-pick efde8a253'; original/trial-4 git-showed it. (c) ANSWER LEAKAGE via network - WebFetch/WebSearch appear in zero transcripts (correctly disabled), but curl to github.com / api.github.com / raw.githubusercontent.com fetched the real PR #14985 diff/patch in naive/trial-4, nodocs/trial-1, nodocs/trial-4, original/trial-2, original/trial-3; the README doc hunk entered context each time (reported above); network egress is evidently not blocked. (d) The naive and original docs snapshots installed by the harness already document the npipe feature the task asks to implement (proven by git show of the snapshot commits) - the worktree README itself leaks the expected doc change. (e) No subagents: zero Task tool calls in all 16 trials, so no sidechain doc access exists. Deliberately NOT reported as consumption: git show/log --stat filename listings, grep -l/-c filename-only output, GitHub API file lists (names and counts, no patch text printed), ls listings naming README.md, the empty-diff for-loop in original/trial-4, and make misspell/checkdoc output echoing doc paths (test/tool output, per instructions). nodocs/trial-2 is genuinely clean: no doc consumption through any channel. approx_chars figures are the measured doc-content portion of the paired tool_result; total output sizes are given in the evidence strings.

per_task.notes: Audit method: parsed all 16 transcripts into tool_use/tool_result maps (924 Bash, 181 Read, 0 Grep, 1 Agent, 10 ToolSearch calls), matched every extractor event for pr-15307 (110 events) to its transcript command, then swept the residue for corpus paths, .md mentions, git readers, indirect channels, tmp-file copies, and network access. Corpus = the 103 files in corpus-manifest.json. KEY SYSTEMIC GAPS: (1) cwd-relative paths — the extractor matches corpus paths literally, so any reader run after `cd cmd/mdatagen` using `internal/.../README.md` or `../../scraper/...` is invisible (the largest class of misses); (2) git show/diff emitting doc content is never captured, even when the literal corpus path appears in the command (original/trial-1); (3) `diff` and `od` are not in the reader regex; (4) tmp-copy laundering (cp doc /tmp/x.md; read /tmp/x.md). NETWORK WAS NOT DISABLED: no WebFetch/WebSearch tool calls exist, and 9 of 16 trials tried to load WebFetch via ToolSearch (all returned 'No matching deferred tools'), but Bash curl egress succeeded across 11+ trials and one Agent subagent (ace/trial-1) relayed a fetched README verbatim. GROUND-TRUTH CONTAMINATION via that egress: the full PR-15307 diff (the task's reference solution, ~3.9-4.0KB) was fetched from patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/github.com in naive/trial-1, ace/trial-4, nodocs/trial-3, and original/trial-3; issue 15306's body ('Remove extra line in README.md') was fetched in ace/trial-3, ace/trial-4, and original/trial-3. Separately, the upstream fix commit dbd5c55bf ('[cmd/mdatagen] Fix the extra blank line in the readme template file') exists in the repos' git history and was git-show'n in ace/trial-3 and naive/trial-3 (readme.md.tmpl is not in the corpus, so these are not listed as missed doc events, but they leak the solution; git show 4db915721 on the same template appeared in 7 trials). Events labeled '(regenerated content)' read a corpus path whose content mdatagen had just rewritten — included for consistency with the extractor, which counts equivalent literal-path reads; discount them if the recount wants pristine-doc consumption only. Doc text echoed in go-test stdout was excluded per instructions. Spot-checks: 4 extractor events verified problematic (see misattributions); 1 verified clean — naive/trial-2 Read of cmd/mdatagen/internal/samplereceiver/README.md, recorded 33686 chars, matches the transcript result exactly. No sidechain Reads exist in any transcript.
